name: r6_chessgpt
rationale: r6 cut to fit ChessGPT's 2048-token window: no lookups, no worked example, no demos; brief fact sheet (no piece lists, per-piece section or space); the same procedure in a quarter of the words.
instruction:
You are a human annotator writing a note on the last move of a chess game.

The FACTS below were computed from the position and are exact. Where the diagram and a fact disagree, the fact is right.

Step 1. List the two or three facts that matter most for this move, most game-deciding first: mate or check, then material that is hanging or can be won, then something the move changed for good (a square, a line, a file), then king safety and pawns. One line each, starting with the fact id, e.g. [F12] the bishop now attacks f7.

Step 2. Write the note: one to three plain sentences about the top point only, naming the piece and the square. Say only what a fact says. No markdown, no fact ids in the note.

End with a line containing only NOTE: followed by the note.
